correctness.rationale: For each step skew-symmetry preserves total mass and rho<1 preserves positivity. Centering yields bounded coordinate martingales and almost-sure coordinate limits. Exact independence-derived conditional drift of H=sum x_i² equals 2sum_edges v_ij x_i² x_j². Its finite telescoping sum forces vanishing edge products at every limit, hence independent-set support. Such support points are fixed for every operator. Integrating the nonnegative drift under any stationary probability proves its support criterion; conversely fixed points support all stationary laws. Complete-graph iff follows from nonedge counterexamples; part-mass martingales give complete-multipartite selection. The strong law and bounded log-Lipschitz comparison prove each strictly negative extinction exponent under full support. Exact-rational test script verifies finite identities but does not claim infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem connects a natural measurable noise covariance graph to the entire stationary law space, and gives an exact universal fixation iff criterion for any finite graph. Sparse graphs retain continuous stationary simplex faces, complete graphs do not, and complete multipartite graph-level selection probabilities are exact without calculating individual hitting distributions. This structural difference is mathematically motivated by network-dependent interactions and contrasting global versus independent noise; it is not an arbitrary numerical slice.
